item.text:
**Verdict**  
Mixed, leaning slightly negative. Srettha made some real welfare-facing moves for broad households, same-sex couples, and border populations, but I did not find strong direct evidence of a sustained, targeted priority for children, the elderly, the disabled, or poor domestic regions. The clearest pattern is broad cash relief plus humanitarian framing, alongside continued repression and limited evidence of deeper social-protection expansion.

**Positive Evidence**
- **Thailand’s cabinet approves $13.5 billion digital wallet handout** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-04-23 | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/thailands-cabinet-approves-135-billion-digital-wallet-handout-3390007) | Claim: Srettha pushed a universal 10,000-baht transfer to 50 million people, which is direct evidence of broad social protection aimed at ordinary households rather than only elites. QIDs: `6B.3`, `6B.2`, `5B.8`
- **Thailand’s $13 billion digital handout scheme to include cash payments, PM says** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-09-03 | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/thai-pm-says-part-of-13-billion-digital-wallet-stimulus-to-be-in-cash-3597164) | Claim: the government later shifted part of the program into cash payments, showing continued concern with household relief and some willingness to adjust delivery. QIDs: `6B.3`, `6B.2`, `5B.9`
- **Thailand advanced a cross-border humanitarian pilot with Myanmar Red Cross participation and AHA Centre technical support** | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | 2024-03-26 | [URL](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/vfm260324-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e) | Claim: Thailand used civilian humanitarian channels to help vulnerable border populations affected by the Myanmar crisis, which is strong evidence of prioritizing people in a threatened region. QIDs: `6B.3`, `6B.2`, `6B.1`
- **Thailand and the ICRC discussed humanitarian assistance to all groups in need in Myanmar without discrimination** | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | 2024-04-26 | [URL](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/vfm-meets-with-icrc-reps-250424-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e) | Claim: the government explicitly framed aid as nondiscriminatory, which supports a welfare-oriented posture toward vulnerable civilians rather than selective favoring. QIDs: `6B.3`, `6B.2`, `6B.1`
- **Thailand’s Senate approved same-sex marriage under Srettha’s government** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-06-18 | [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/06/18/victory-same-sex-marriage-thailand) | Claim: a major excluded group gained equal civil status in 2024, making this one of the clearest positive priority signals for marginalized communities. QIDs: `6B.3`, `6B.1`, `5B.8`
- **Thailand’s House passed the Marriage Equality Act by an overwhelming margin under Srettha’s government** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-03-27 | [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/27/thailand-promptly-pass-same-sex-marriage-bill) | Claim: this is concrete support for an excluded group, but it looks like a discrete legislative win rather than a broad vulnerability-focused social agenda. QIDs: `6B.3`, `6B.1`, `5B.8`
- **Thailand brought no reports of internet shutdowns, but civil liberties remained constrained** | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | [URL](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/thailand) | Claim: media criticism and some pluralism remained available, which is only weak positive evidence that vulnerable voices were not entirely excluded from public debate. QIDs: `6B.3`, `6B.1`, `6B.2`

**Negative Evidence**
- **Thailand last-ditch effort for Tak Bai justice** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-05-01 | [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/05/01/thailand-last-ditch-effort-tak-bai-massacre-justice) | Claim: persistent impunity for deadly abuses against a Muslim minority and a restive border region undercuts any claim that Srettha strongly prioritized marginalized communities. QIDs: `6B.3`, `6B.1`, `5B.8`, `5B.9`
- **Thailand swap mart targets foreign dissidents, refugees** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-05-15 | [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/05/15/thailand-swap-mart-targets-foreign-dissidents-refugees) | Claim: harassment, surveillance, and forced returns against dissidents and refugees are strong evidence against equal concern for vulnerable and marginalized groups. QIDs: `6B.3`, `6B.1`, `5B.8`
- **Thailand new government slow to protect rights** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-11 | [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/thailand-new-government-slow-protect-rights) | Claim: HRW said the new government was still pursuing politically motivated prosecutions of peaceful protesters and monarchy critics, showing weak protection for unpopular groups. QIDs: `6B.3`, `6B.1`, `5B.8`
- **Thailand’s flagship $14 billion handout faces delays, snags and criticism** | Reuters via Yahoo News | 2024-08-01 | [URL](https://www.yahoo.com/news/thailands-flagship-14-billion-handout-072635149.html) | Claim: implementation snags and fiscal-risk criticism show the biggest welfare-style measure was not yet delivering reliably to households. QIDs: `6B.3`, `6B.2`, `5B.9`
- **Thailand’s cabinet approves $13.5 billion digital wallet handout** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-04-23 | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/thailands-cabinet-approves-135-billion-digital-wallet-handout-3390007) | Claim: the plan was broad and popular, but its scale and controversy also make it look like a politically salient universal payout rather than a sharply targeted vulnerable-groups program. QIDs: `6B.3`, `6B.2`, `5B.9`
- **Thailand’s official stance on universal rights and inclusive societies** | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | 2024-02-28 | [URL](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/statement-vfm-280224?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c3060006848) | Claim: the rhetoric was inclusive, but it is still rhetoric; I found little direct evidence that this translated into major targeted programs for children, the elderly, the disabled, or poor regions. QIDs: `6B.3`, `6B.1`

**Gap**
I found solid evidence for broad household cash relief, humanitarian border assistance, and same-sex marriage, but little direct 2024 evidence of targeted gains for children, elderly people, disabled people, housing, water/sanitation, or poor domestic regions. The biggest missing piece is sustained, specific policy delivery for those groups rather than general or symbolic inclusion.
